slot.brief: Particle with given position and velocity vectors; compute angular momentum about the origin via L = r × p.

stem: A particle of mass $2$ kg has position vector $\vec{r} = (\hat{i} + 2\hat{j})$ m and velocity $\vec{v} = (3\hat{i} - 4\hat{j})$ m s$^{-1}$. The angular momentum of the particle about the origin is:
working:
$\vec{p} = m\vec{v} = 2(3\hat{i} - 4\hat{j}) = 6\hat{i} - 8\hat{j}$ kg m s$^{-1}$.
$\vec{L} = \vec{r} \times \vec{p} = (\hat{i} + 2\hat{j})\times(6\hat{i} - 8\hat{j}) = \hat{i}\times(-8\hat{j}) + 2\hat{j}\times 6\hat{i} = -8\hat{k} -12\hat{k} = -20\hat{k}$ kg m$^2$ s$^{-1}$.

Independent check: \(\vec L=\vec r\times m\vec v\), so \(L_z=1(-8)-2(6)=-20\).
solution: Angular momentum is $\vec L=\vec r\times m\vec v$, with $m\vec v=6\hat i-8\hat j$.\n$$\vec L=(\hat i+2\hat j)\times(6\hat i-8\hat j)=(-8-12)\hat k=-20\hat k\ \text{kg m}^2\text{s}^{-1}.$$
